standard.title: Create and present texts for diverse contexts
standard.description: create and present informative and imaginative texts for diverse contexts and purposes, selecting vocabulary, expressions, sentence structures and textual features and conventions, to engage different audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create spoken, written and multimodal informative and imaginative texts for purpose and audience (AC9LCH8EC05). They have drafted, revised and produced texts for community audiences. They have not yet created evaluative and persuasive texts at extended length, produced formal procedural or policy-based texts, or created literary texts drawing on specific target language literary traditions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and present informative and imaginative texts for diverse contexts — including evaluative, persuasive, procedural and literary forms — selecting language and conventions deliberately to engage different audiences.

nodes.label: Evaluative and persuasive texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce evaluative and persuasive texts — issue analyses, debate speeches, community presentations — using evidence, balanced perspective and persuasive language structures.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce an evaluative or persuasive text of at least ten sentences with a clear position, at least two pieces of supporting evidence, and at least two persuasive structures.
nodes.typical_width: Create presentations on contemporary issues analysing pros and cons; produce persuasive texts for community audiences; write evaluations comparing alternative positions; present on population, environmental, educational or community issues; use statistical data and research evidence.
wider: Produce an extended persuasive text on a topic of genuine community relevance, with a documented drafting and revision process showing deliberate language choices
Compare persuasive text conventions in target language and English — identify how argument structure, evidence use and rhetorical strategy differ across the two languages
nodes.hinge_reason: Evaluative and persuasive text production is the foundational capability for all advanced text creation at Y9-10. Students who can only produce narrative or informative texts cannot meet the analytical and advocacy production demands that follow.

response_modes.reason: Persuasive text production requires deliberate structural planning — position, evidence, counter-argument, conclusion. Explicit argument structure instruction followed by scaffolded production builds the planning capacity that produces genuinely persuasive texts.

success_criteria: Produces an evaluative or persuasive text with a clear position supported by at least two pieces of evidence
Uses at least two persuasive structures across the text

nodes.label: Multimodal community and cultural texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce multimodal texts — presentations, exhibitions, cultural performances, community resources — combining spoken, written and visual elements for specific community audiences.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a multimodal text combining at least two modes for a community or cultural audience, with deliberate mode selection justified by audience and purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Produce multimodal presentations using data and statistics; compose texts for events with specific purposes; create cultural exhibitions and performances; write voice-overs and scripts for drama or comedy; create resources for Chinese-speaking community audiences; reflect on co-creating Acknowledgements of Country with First Nations Australians.
wider: Create a multimodal community text for a real audience — evaluate its effectiveness with that audience and revise based on feedback
Produce a cultural performance or exhibition that draws on a specific target language cultural tradition — explain the cultural choices made and how they serve the audience

response_modes.reason: Multimodal community text production requires students to understand how different modes serve different purposes for different audiences. Practice across varied production formats — exhibitions, performances, presentations, community resources — builds the flexible multimodal production capacity needed.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students bring cultural knowledge and community connections that give multimodal community production tasks genuine depth and authenticity. Width investment here creates the conditions for community-facing work that has real cultural value.
success_criteria: Produces a multimodal text combining at least two modes for a community or cultural audience
Demonstrates deliberate mode selection appropriate to audience and purpose

nodes.label: Literary and formal texts using stylistic models
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create literary and formal texts using stylistic models — applying target language literary conventions, experimenting with formal language, and producing texts that demonstrate deliberate stylistic choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a literary or formal text applying at least two conventions from a specific target language literary or formal style, with at least one deliberate stylistic choice explained.
nodes.typical_width: Write narratives about characters from books or films; write biographies of significant figures using literary language; create scripts for short plays or video clips; experiment with formal versus subjective language; use literary style models; compose texts for school publications and community contexts.
wider: Create a text in a specific target language literary style — apply the conventions authentically and annotate the stylistic choices made
Reflect on the production process — explain what cultural knowledge was required to apply the literary conventions and what was learned about the target language literary tradition

response_modes.reason: Literary and formal text creation integrates evaluative writing skills (node 1) and multimodal production (node 2) into the fullest expression of creative and formal capability at Y9-10. The teaching investment is in creating genuine literary engagement — students as authors with a vision, not only genre followers.

success_criteria: Creates a literary or formal text applying at least two conventions from a specific style
Explains at least one deliberate stylistic choice made
